fields.statement: QA with the branch build (go build ./cmd/rhiza) in a scratch Rhiza root, fake rex, RHIZA_TEST_DETACH_LOG: one milestone change set and two backlog change sets with leaves. rhiza daemon --once --max-runs=3 with no policy.toml started milestone first then backlog; backlog = "before" started backlog first; backlog = "skip" started only the milestone one and daemon status listed each backlog one as 'serves no milestone'; backlog = "x" did the same with the policy error as the skip detail (text and --json reason no-milestone). Backlog order follows acceptance time, not ID: a change set made first but accepted later started second.

QA with the branch build: rhiza daemon --once with a fake rex picks the milestone change set with a leaf under every backlog value, and backlog change sets only by the [schedule] backlog rule (after/before/skip/unknown checked by hand), each start logged once as rhiza run start --foreground <cs>.

QA with the branch build: rhiza check on a scratch repo fails with 'fail policy .rhiza/policy.toml: schedule.backlog "sometimes" is not one of "after", "before" or "skip"', fails on malformed TOML with 'fail policy .rhiza/policy.toml: toml: line 2: ...', and reports no policy problem with backlog = "before" or no file.

QA with the branch build as rhiza on PATH, the plan-milestone-check.txtar fixtures (fake claude/rex/gh) run by hand: rhiza run start --workflow plan on a plan serving an intent under no milestone ended failed at milestone-check naming the change set and policy.toml's backlog = "skip" when that file was present, and with no policy.toml passed milestone-check, entered review and the run succeeded.

QA with the branch build, plan run by hand with fake agents: milestone-check passes a plan serving no milestone with no policy.toml (run goes on to review and succeeds) and fails it, never reaching review, with backlog = "skip", printing the change set and the fix.

QA with the branch build: rhiza guide plan says to link a milestone only when RHIZA_MILESTONE names one or an open milestone fits, that other work is built as backlog by .rhiza/policy.toml's [schedule] backlog rule, and that under "skip" the serves link must reach a milestone.

QA with the branch build: rhiza guide plan names RHIZA_MILESTONE, links a milestone only when set or one fits, names .rhiza/policy.toml's backlog rule and its "skip" exception, and no longer says every change set must serve a milestone.
